header.userPrompt:
Add optional per-account nicknames (aliases) to bank statements.

## Problem
A user can hold several cards at the same bank. Statements only distinguish them by the last 4 digits, which is hard to tell apart. Let the user attach an optional, human-friendly nickname to an "account" and surface it in the UI.

## Concept — there is no account entity today
An "account" is the tuple (bank_name, product_type, account_last4, currency) — the same 5-tuple key the overlap detection already uses in server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/daos/BankStatementDAO.scala (findOverlapping, overlappingStatementIds). The frontend currently derives an account grouping key in web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/bankstatements/BankStatementsLogic.scala (accountKey) and a display label in BankStatementsPage.scala (accountLabelOf). Do NOT introduce an account foreign key on bank_statement; the alias is a side lookup only.

## Data model
Add a new Play evolution (the next number after the latest file in server/src/main/resources/evolutions/default/). Table `bank_account_alias`:
- id UUID NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY
- user_id UUID NOT NULL, FK -> users(user_id)
- bank_name TEXT NOT NULL
- product_type TEXT NOT NULL
- account_last4 TEXT NOT NULL
- currency TEXT NOT NULL
- alias TEXT NOT NULL      -- may be the empty string; never null
- created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL
- updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL
- UNIQUE (user_id, bank_name, product_type, account_last4, currency)
- index on user_id

No CHECK constraints and no column DEFAULTs (app-level validation only, per repo conventions). The table stores ONLY the key tuple plus the alias — no other per-account settings.

## Behaviour
1. Ensure-at-confirm: in ConfirmBankStatementDraftAction's confirm path, inside the SAME transaction that creates the statement + rows (extend the repository method behind createConfirmedStatement), ensure a bank_account_alias row exists for the confirmed statement's tuple with an empty alias (""), only if one does not already exist. NEVER overwrite an existing alias.
2. Set-alias endpoint keyed by a STATEMENT id (not the tuple): the server loads the statement user-scoped, derives its tuple, and upserts the alias row (create if missing, update the alias if present). An empty alias is allowed and must be stored as-is. NEVER delete the row. Enforce a 60-character maximum app-side and return a validation error if exceeded. A statement id that is not the authenticated user's returns not found.
3. Reading: left-join the alias into the statement reads so each statement in the GetBankStatements list response and the GetBankStatement response carries its optional alias. A missing row or an empty alias string both mean "no nickname".

## Rendering
Keep the existing default label exactly as it is today (bank (product) dot-dot-dot-dot last4). When a non-empty alias exists, render it as `<alias> (<existing default label>)`. Put this in ONE shared label function that the list dropdown, the account selector, the per-account timeline, and the statement review header all call, so every surface agrees.

## Edit UI — both locations
- The statement review/detail header (web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/bankstatementreview/).
- The list page's account selector (web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/bankstatements/BankStatementsPage.scala).
In each, show the current alias and an inline control to edit it. Autofocus the input when the edit opens (useEffect + ref), and wrap it in an HTML form with onSubmit so Enter submits. Make the copy clear that the nickname applies to the whole account (every statement of that card), not to the single statement being viewed.

## Conventions (must follow)
- Tapir endpoint definitions live in lib/api/shared/ and are shared by both sides; wire controller -> thin action -> Anorm repository/DAO.
- Every DB query, read and write, includes WHERE user_id = ?. Every list query has an ORDER BY.
- Use Chimney (transformInto / into.transform) for case-class shape mapping instead of hand-copying fields.
- No external API calls in tests; follow docs/guide/testing.md.
- New API gets explicit length/count limits (the 60-char alias limit here).
- Frontend reachability: the edit control must be reachable and usable in the running UI, not just wired in the router.
- Public repository: NO personally identifying data anywhere in code, tests, comments, fixtures, or the PR text — no real bank names, account numbers, filenames, merchant names, or amounts. Use neutral placeholders.
- The PR description must NOT contain any claude.ai session link.

## Tests to add/adjust
- DAO: upsert create, upsert update, empty-alias stored as "", 60-char boundary accept + over-limit reject, and user-scoping (another user's tuple is isolated).
- Confirm flow: ensures an empty-alias row for the tuple and does not clobber an existing alias.
- Set-alias action: create, update, set-to-empty, over-length rejection, and wrong-user returns not found.
- The shared label function: alias set vs empty vs absent.

## Acceptance criteria
- A user can set, change, and clear (to empty) a nickname for an account from BOTH the statement review header and the list account selector; it persists and appears on every statement of that account.
- Confirming a statement ensures an empty-alias account row exists for its tuple without overwriting an existing alias.
- An alias longer than 60 characters is rejected with a validation error.
- All reads and writes are user-scoped; another user's statement id can neither set nor read an alias.
- The full test suite passes.
